root_cause.text: In KVM’s AMD SVM nested virtualization path, `nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02()` failed to copy the CPU-updated `int_state` interrupt-shadow bit from `vmcb02` into the cached `vmcb12`, so nested state save/restore could restore an incorrect interrupt shadow depending on ioctl ordering.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `svm->nested.ctl.int_state = svm->vmcb->control.int_state;` in `arch/x86/kvm/svm/nested.c`, and the CVE description says `int_state` “is also written by the CPU, specifically bit 0 ... but it is not sync'd to cached vmcb12,” causing `KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE` / `KVM_SET_VCPU_EVENTS` ordering to restore the interrupt shadow into the wrong VMCB and potentially hang L2.

intent_record.intent_summary: Sync `int_state` from vmcb02 into nested control state to preserve correct interrupt handling in nested virtualization.
intent_record.what: A new assignment copies `svm->vmcb->control.int_state` into `svm->nested.ctl.int_state` inside `nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02(struct vcpu_svm *svm)`, alongside the existing copies of `event_inj` and `event_inj_err`.
intent_record.how: This causes the nested VMCB control interrupt state to be synchronized from vmcb02 into the nested control structure, so nested virtualization preserves the current interrupt state instead of leaving it stale or uninitialized.

grouping_result.intent: Sync `int_state` from vmcb02 into nested control state to preserve correct interrupt handling in nested virtualization.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes nested SVM state synchronization by copying the CPU-updated int_state interrupt-shadow bit from vmcb02 into the cached nested state, which prevents incorrect restore behavior.

candidates.rationale: This code copies selected nested control state from vmcb02 into the cached vmcb12, but the pre-fix path omitted the CPU-updated int_state interrupt-shadow bit. As a result, nested save/restore could preserve stale interrupt shadow state depending on ioctl ordering.

This is part of the same synchronization sequence for nested control state. The root cause is that the routine failed to synchronize int_state alongside these fields, allowing incorrect interrupt-shadow restoration.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is one of the vmcb02-to-vmcb12 synchronization statements in nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02(). The vulnerability is that the routine failed to copy the CPU-updated int_state interrupt-shadow bit into the cached nested control state, so this line is part of the incomplete state synchronization that allowed stale interrupt shadow to be restored.

This line is part of the same synchronization block in nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02(). Because int_state was not copied alongside the other nested control fields, nested state save/restore could preserve an incorrect interrupt-shadow bit depending on ioctl ordering.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit

The control state changes on every L2->L0
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 2d8a42be0e2b15a4e0b20349f27bb8288db5ebe6
Author: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Date:   Fri May 22 03:50:14 2020 -0400

    KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit
    
    The control state changes on every L2->L0 vmexit, and we will have to
    serialize it in the nested state.  So keep it up to date in svm->nested.ctl
    and just copy them back to the nested VMCB in nested_svm_vmexit.
    
    Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this snippet: the old code that directly copied only parts of control state from `vmcb->control` into `nested_vmcb->control` is removed, and the new helper `sync_nested_vmcb_control()` explicitly synchronizes processor-updated control fields into the cached nested state. In particular, it updates `svm->nested.ctl.event_inj` and `svm->nested.ctl.int_ctl` from `svm->vmcb->control` with masking logic (`svm->nested.ctl.int_ctl &= ~mask; svm->nested.ctl.int_ctl |= svm->vmcb->control.int_ctl & mask;`). Then `nested_svm_vmexit()` copies the cached values back: `nested_vmcb->control.int_ctl = svm->nested.ctl.int_ctl;`, `nested_vmcb->control.event_inj = svm->nested.ctl.event_inj;`, and `nested_vmcb->control.event_inj_err = svm->nested.ctl.event_inj_err;`. This shows the fix is already present and the previous unsynchronized restore path is no longer used here.
